scope.description: Review-first refresh of ten published launch-era company profiles with generic capability records and insufficient decision context.

source.title: Norsat satellite terminals
source.locator: Portable, maritime, fixed and vehicle-mounted terminal portfolio
source.summary: Norsat describes fly-away, maritime, fixed, and drive-away satellite terminals across multiple frequency bands, with rugged construction and remote terminal-control features.

leads.evidenceLocator: Portable, maritime, fixed and vehicle-mounted terminal portfolio
followUpQuestions: Verify the exact terminal, band and antenna configuration, modem and network interfaces, accreditation, environmental tests, delivered military references, contested-link performance, stock position, and support model.
reviewWarnings: The public product catalogue does not establish configuration-specific defence accreditation, current military contracts, field availability, throughput under contested conditions, interoperability certification, or support lead times.

recoveryAttempts.outcome: Resolved a concrete capability delta against the exact live organization and capability baseline.
Checked official government, customer, partner, or organization material for independent proof and attribution limits.
Checked Canadian English and French terminology and retained only durable public evidence with portable URLs.

leads.refreshSummary: Replace the generic launch-era capability for Norsat International with a cited and decision-useful capability definition.
intendedChanges: Update only the existing capability's name, summary, type, features, applications, and technical tags after review.

source.title: Aurora launch vehicle
source.locator: Aurora stages, payload, propulsion, fairing and mission architecture
source.summary: Reaction Dynamics describes Aurora as a two-stage hybrid launch vehicle with stated low-Earth and sun-synchronous payload classes, containerized support, and restartable upper-stage propulsion.

leads.evidenceLocator: Aurora stages, payload, propulsion, fairing and mission architecture
followUpQuestions: Verify current test and flight milestones, propulsion qualification, licensing, launch-site integration, payload performance, schedule and funding, production readiness, and independently observed mission results.
reviewWarnings: Company timelines for suborbital and orbital service are forward-looking; public evidence does not establish completed flight qualification, achieved orbital launch, launch licence, demonstrated payload performance, production cadence, or defence customer adoption.
